findings.title: Source of truth for the copilot compilation is ambiguous and one reading breaks a parent success criterion
findings.description: The file-layout block says instruction files come "from `.claude/rules/typescript.md`" and prompt files "from `.claude/skills/commit.md`" — i.e. the copilot backend reads CF's *generated* Claude artifacts. The existing guide script does not work that way: its `claude` case compiles from `$SCRIPT_DIR/../project-guides/rules` (verified in `project-documents/scripts/setup-ide`), and its cursor/windsurf cases copy that same rules dir — no backend reads `.claude/`. If the copilot backend takes `.claude/` as input, then `cf setup-ide copilot` on a fresh project produces nothing, which contradicts the slice-plan success criterion "`cf init --ide copilot` runs end-to-end on a fresh directory: git init, project create, guide install, setup-ide copilot" (no claude step in that sequence). Worse, that premise is already unsound: the only skill in this repo is `.claude/skills/analyze/SKILL.md` (a subdirectory), while `propagateToWorktrees` copies `entry.isFile()` at the top level of each dir, so `.claude/skills/*` yields zero files today and no flat `.claude/skills/commit.md` exists to translate. Fix the design by naming one source (`project-guides/rules/` + `project-guides/agents/` in the guide, mirroring the claude backend) and by defining the actual skill input shape (`<name>/SKILL.md`, whose frontmatter carries `name`/`description`/`disable-model-invocation`, not `argument-hint`/`agent`/`model`/`tools`).

findings.title: Managed-marker safety gate covers 2 of 4 output locations and leaves mixed states undefined
findings.description: Step 4 checks only `.github/copilot-instructions.md` and `AGENTS.md`. The slice also writes `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` and `.github/prompts/*.prompt.md`, and users demonstrably own files in that space (`.github/` routinely holds `workflows/`, `ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, and hand-written instruction files). Those per-file outputs can be silently overwritten or clobbered by a run with no prompt and no backup, which does not satisfy the plan's "same safety as Claude path." The design also never defines the partial states: managed `AGENTS.md` with unmanaged `copilot-instructions.md`, or one of the two present and the other absent. Related, and unaddressed: with per-file emission there is no pruning story — a rule removed from the source leaves a stale `.instructions.md` forever, whereas the claude path sidesteps this by rewriting `CLAUDE.md` wholesale each run. Enumerate the gate over all four targets (or state why per-file targets need none), specify mixed-state behavior, and say whether the backend clears/prunes generated files it no longer emits.

findings.title: Cross-repo guide coupling has no sequencing or version-preflight strategy
findings.description: The design correctly names this "the highest-risk coupling" but the handling is "it will fail at the script step with a clear error." Verified in the workspace copy of `setup-ide`, an unknown target hits `case cursor|windsurf|claude) … *) exit 1` and CF surfaces it as `setup-ide exited with code 1` — so the failure is loud, but the user gets no "update your guides to vX" hint, and `cf init --ide copilot` (which runs with `{ yes: true }`) will report a warn line and continue to the "project is ready" summary. The coupling is also already drifting in the other direction: the guide script supports `cursor`/`windsurf` while `VALID_TARGETS` does not, so the doc's claim that a new target is "add an entry to `VALID_TARGETS`, add a backend" is not the whole story. Name the required guide version/feature gate (a minimum-version check via the existing `GuideDetector` version data, or an explicit feature probe before invoking the script) and state that the guide-side change lands and tags before the CLI change, since this slice's `dependencies:` frontmatter is `[]`.

findings.title: Parent onboarding NFR is not restated although the slice adds work to that path
findings.description: The parent architecture states the initiative-level target: "from `npm install` to useful context output in under two minutes." `cf init --ide copilot` is on that exact path and adds a second `execFileSync('bash', …, { stdio: 'inherit' })` compilation over every rules file plus four directory/file writes. The slice restates nothing about that budget and offers no target or verification, so the requirement the gap leaves unmet is the parent's stated first-run latency goal for non-Claude users. Restate the target in the slice doc (e.g. "copilot compilation must not push `cf init --ide copilot` beyond the parent's two-minute first-run budget") and note how it is checked in the existing timing/manual verification step.

findings.title: Highest-risk logic has no test coverage or stated verification owner
findings.description: All seven listed tests are CF-side target validation, safety-prompt, and propagation checks. The plan's success criterion "Path→applyTo translation correctly converts Claude frontmatter to Copilot frontmatter" has no corresponding test, and neither does the skills→prompt frontmatter mapping. Since translation lives in the guide script, CF-side tests structurally cannot cover it — so the design must say where it *is* covered (guide-script tests, or an explicit manual-verification checklist with the real emitted fixture). This matters more than usual given the input forms the project guide warns about: real rule files here use `paths:` arrays, and some have trailing space after `paths:` (`react.md`, `sql.md`, `testing.md`) plus inline-style values in `typescript.md`; a translator that requires one exact YAML layout will silently emit `applyTo: "**"` or nothing.

findings.title: Dual-writing `AGENTS.md` adds a third copy of the compiled rules with no divergence policy
findings.description: The rationale (cross-tool compatibility) is sound and matches the tool guide, but the consequence is not addressed: `cf setup-ide claude` regenerates `CLAUDE.md` and `cf setup-ide copilot` regenerates `AGENTS.md` + `copilot-instructions.md` from the same source, so a project running both commands diverges the moment either is run after a rule change. Either state that both backends refresh all three managed files, or cut the `AGENTS.md` write — the tool guide notes VS Code also reads `CLAUDE.md` in compatibility mode, so `copilot-instructions.md` alone meets the slice's stated requirement for Copilot users.

findings.title: Naming and mechanism inconsistencies in the Files Changed list
findings.description: The helper appears as `isManagedCopilot(filePath)` in Technical Scope and `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)` in Files Changed — pick one, since the shape difference (per-file vs per-project) is exactly what the mixed-state gap above needs to resolve. Separately, "Update CLI help text to list both targets" is already automatic: `.argument('<target>', \`IDE target: ${VALID_TARGETS.join(', ')}\`)` derives the string from the constant, so that scope item can be dropped.

findings.title: Worktree propagation for the new dirs should not repeat the top-level-files-only pattern
findings.description: The existing claude propagation copies only `entry.isFile()` in each directory, and the tool guide says VS Code searches `.github/instructions` recursively. If the copilot backend ever emits nested instruction files, a copied-per-dir-block will silently omit them. A single sentence constraining the emitted layout to flat files (or specifying recursive copy) closes this.
